metadata.title: The effects of teaching initiative, ICT application, and teaching collaboration on teachers’ creative thinking: Latent profile and multiple logistic regression analysis

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the PISA 2022 Teacher Questionnaire (International Option) and applies the teacher-level sampling weight WTTEACH to address PISA’s stratified two-stage cluster sampling (schools sampled proportional to size; teachers sampled within schools). In the data processing stage, the authors compute WLE (Weighted Likelihood Estimation) scores for key teacher scales and explicitly state that WLE integrates psychometric calibration with WTTEACH to correct for sampling bias and non-response/unequal sampling probabilities across regions and schools. In the Mplus analyses, the authors also use TYPE=COMPLEX to adjust standard errors for school-level clustering of teachers within schools, together with WTTEACH. The paper does not report replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so uncertainty estimation relies on the complex-survey adjustment rather than replicate designs.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2022 Teacher Questionnaire (International Option) teacher-level data and restricted the analytic sample to teachers in Hong Kong and Macao Special Administrative Regions. The initial total sample size was 4251 teachers, then excluded cases with missing values on control variables and on the three key creative-thinking variables (openness to creativity, creative values, creative pedagogies) when all three were missing (Missing=99). Region and subject were treated as having no missing values, and the final analytic sample comprised 4069 teachers.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Teacher Questionnaire (International Option) — Hong Kong & Macao teachers
main_findings.target_variable: Teachers’ creative thinking class membership (5-class LPA outcome)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Latent Profile Analysis: optimal 5-class solution (C-5) with highest entropy=0.93; BLRT and LMRT significant for 2–5 classes (p<.001). Multiple logistic regression (vs Class 1 reference): Teaching initiative ORs for Class 3/4/5 = 1.397/1.526/1.893 (all p<.001); ICT application ORs for Class 2/3/4/5 = 1.148/1.336/1.524/1.726 (p<.05 to p<.001); Teaching collaboration ORs for Class 3/4/5 = 1.211/1.266/1.613 (p<.05 to p<.001).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Teacher Questionnaire (International Option) data from Hong Kong and Macao teachers, the study leveraged Gender, Age, Region, Subject, and Teaching initiative (autonomy) to model teachers’ creative thinking class membership, finding that higher teaching initiative, ICT application, and teaching collaboration significantly increased the odds of belonging to higher creative-thinking classes (e.g., Teaching initiative OR=1.893 for the highest class). This indicates that teacher-support policies that strengthen autonomy, purposeful ICT use, and collaborative professional learning may shift teachers toward higher creative-thinking profiles, though the cross-sectional design limits causal claims.

data.outcome_summary: This study analyzed PISA 2022 Teacher Questionnaire (International Option) data restricted to teachers in Hong Kong and Macao Special Administrative Regions (final N=4069; HKG=2165, MAC=1904). Teachers’ creative thinking was operationalized as three WLE-scaled dimensions (openness to creativity, creative values, creative pedagogies) and classified via Latent Profile Analysis, yielding an optimal 5-class solution (C-5) with entropy=0.93 and significant BLRT/LMRT (p<.001). Multiple logistic regression then explained membership in each creative-thinking class (reference: Class 1) using Gender, Age, Region, Subject, Teaching initiative, ICT application, and Teaching collaboration, with key gradient effects: Teaching initiative OR=1.397/1.526/1.893 for Classes 3/4/5 (p<.001), ICT application OR=1.148/1.336/1.524/1.726 for Classes 2–5 (p<.05 to p<.001), and Teaching collaboration OR=1.211/1.266/1.613 for Classes 3–5 (p<.05 to p<.001). The paper uses WLE (not PVs) and handles missingness via FIML in Mplus with TYPE=COMPLEX for school clustering; however, the design is cross-sectional and correlational, so reverse causality and response bias remain plausible limitations.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The study does not train or evaluate machine-learning predictive models (no supervised ML algorithms such as Random Forest/XGBoost/SVM are reported). Instead, it uses person-centered Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) to form latent classes and then applies multiple logistic regression to interpret class membership; therefore, the ML technique fields are intentionally left empty. Because the paper is not an empirical predictive ML study, there are no ML performance metrics (e.g., AUC/RMSE) to extract beyond model-fit indices for LPA and odds ratios from logistic regression.
